provenance.description: D1 timber-framed wall kit (K1): lime-plastered oak bays (plain, window, door, braced), the corner post, limestone plinth runs, iron, glass, foot soil and plants, with the two-storey test house layout. Every texel and vertex is generated by the project's seeded Blender/NumPy scripts; no image, scan or third-party material is sampled.

generation.tool: Blender 5.2.1 LTS (headless) with bundled NumPy; Node meshoptimizer 1.2.0 and KTX-Software 4.4.2
generation.author: Claude (Anthropic) under human direction
generation.lineage: source candidate 18 (human-accepted 2026-09-26) -> source candidate 19 (front-left corner fixed at the human's direction, staged on ground to the horizon; human-accepted 2026-09-27) -> delivery candidate 4 (low-passed displaced LODs, BC1/BC7 maps, geometric plaster AO with the real facade neighbours; human-accepted 2026-09-27, K1 delivery step 1) -> source candidate 20 (mitred, pegged corner braces and closed corner slots at the human's direction; human-accepted 2026-09-27) -> delivery candidate 5 (candidate 4's pipeline on source candidate 20)

rightsReview.basis: All geometry and maps (plaster, oak, stone, iron, glass, soil, plants) are generated from seeds by project-authored scripts licensed Apache-2.0. The generated concept references were only viewed for comparison; none of their pixels, and no scan, photograph, third-party texture or model, is an input. The timber-framed building type is a common historical vernacular; no third-party design is reproduced. The review supports project public-build use.
